findings.text: the paragraph states the table gives every test's verdict at each arm and names only two tests as not run, but the table itself (lines 42-44) records three tests with no verdict at either arm and a fourth whose base arm never started, so the done_when clause asking for every other test's verdict beside its base verdict is unmet for three of the five rows; the table rows are accurate and label the gaps, so this is an overstatement in the prose rather than a false claim.

the head failure is attributed to 'the known 550 stall and not this node's' on the strength of the carrier loading as a store hit, but no base arm ran for that test (arms-head-base.log line 239-254 ends with the job cancelled EXIT=15) and the stall residual the plan records for the limited 550 cold solve was 5.681e-3, not the 1.444e-4 measured here; the attribution is plausible and the fixture is demonstrably serving, but it is not established by this run.

the manifest carries no baseline_suite or after_suite JSON block although the run brief required both, so added failures cannot be read from the record; the two arms are recoverable only by parsing arms-head-base.log, whose base arm stops at the cancelled limited-550 row, which is why no failure is attributable as added rather than pre-existing.
